_note: Draft v0 by Claude for quantrungvu (2026-10-10). Jerry reviews and edits. The id of each rule is the mistake 'tag' used by the AI, the stats and the coach: change an id only together with tests/sentences.json. focus_pos = which kinds of target words are good practice for the rule (used by the coach's 'Practise this' button). Keep a rule with id 'other'.

rules.title: Le/la, un/une (gender)
rules.rule: Every French noun is masculine or feminine. Use un/le with masculine nouns and une/la with feminine nouns.

rules.title: Missing article
rules.rule: French nouns almost always need an article (le, la, un, une, des, du…), even where English has none.

rules.title: Du, de la, des (some)
rules.rule: For an amount you don't count, use du, de la or de l'. After a negation, use de or d'.
rules.wrong: Je ne mange pas du pain.
rules.right: Je ne mange pas de pain.

rules.title: Au, aux, du, des
rules.rule: à + le becomes au, à + les becomes aux, de + le becomes du, de + les becomes des.

rules.title: J', l', d' before a vowel
rules.rule: Je, le, la, de, ne and que drop their last vowel before a word starting with a vowel or a silent h.

rules.title: Être (to be)
rules.rule: Être is irregular: je suis, tu es, il/elle/on est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont.

rules.title: Avoir (to have) and age
rules.rule: Avoir is irregular: j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont. French uses avoir for age: j'ai 20 ans.

rules.title: -er verbs in the present
rules.rule: Regular -er verbs end in -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent.

rules.title: Irregular verbs in the present
rules.rule: Common verbs like aller, faire, prendre, venir, vouloir and pouvoir are irregular: learn their forms (je vais, je fais, je prends…).

rules.title: Verb matches the subject
rules.rule: The verb ending must match who does the action (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils).

rules.title: Adjective matches the noun
rules.rule: Adjectives change with the noun: add -e for feminine and -s for plural (petit, petite, petits, petites).

rules.title: Where the adjective goes
rules.rule: Most adjectives go after the noun. A few short common ones go before: beau, bon, grand, petit, jeune, vieux, nouveau.

rules.title: Ne … pas
rules.rule: To say 'not', put ne before the verb and pas after it: je ne mange pas.

rules.title: Asking questions
rules.rule: Ask with a rising voice (Tu viens ?), with est-ce que (Est-ce que tu viens ?), or with a question word (Où est-ce que tu habites ?).

rules.title: À, en, au + places
rules.rule: Use à with cities (à Paris), en with most feminine countries (en France), au with masculine countries (au Japon), dans for inside a place.

rules.title: Mon, ma, mes
rules.rule: Mon/ma/mes match the thing owned, not the owner: mon père, ma mère, mes amis. Use mon before a feminine word starting with a vowel: mon amie.

rules.title: Word order
rules.rule: The usual order is subject + verb + rest. Short adverbs like souvent and bien usually come right after the verb.

rules.title: Fixed prepositions
rules.rule: Some verbs and expressions always take the same preposition: avoir besoin de, penser à, jouer au (sport) / du (instrument).

rules.title: Aller + infinitive (near future)
rules.rule: To talk about the near future, use aller in the present + a verb in the infinitive: je vais manger.

rules.title: Avoir or être in the past
rules.rule: Most verbs use avoir in the passé composé. Movement verbs like aller, venir, partir, arriver, sortir, rester use être.

rules.title: Past participle form
rules.rule: Use the right past participle (mangé, fini, pris, fait) and, with être, add -e/-s to match the subject.

rules.title: Object pronouns (le, la, lui, en, y)
rules.rule: Object pronouns go before the verb: je le mange, j'y vais, j'en veux.

rules.title: Imparfait or passé composé
rules.rule: Use the imparfait for background and habits in the past (il faisait beau), and the passé composé for a finished action (je suis sorti).
rules.wrong: Quand j'étais petit, j'ai joué au foot tous les jours.
rules.right: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au foot tous les jours.

rules.title: Comparing (plus, moins, aussi … que)
rules.rule: Compare with plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que. Bon becomes meilleur.
rules.wrong: Ce café est plus bon que l'autre.
rules.right: Ce café est meilleur que l'autre.

rules.title: Qui or que
rules.rule: Use qui when the next word is a verb (the person who does), que when a new subject follows (the thing that I see).
rules.wrong: Le livre qui je lis est bon.
rules.right: Le livre que je lis est bon.

rules.title: Si + imparfait, conditionnel
rules.rule: For an imagined situation: si + imparfait, then the conditional: si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.
rules.wrong: Si j'aurais le temps, je voyagerais.
rules.right: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.

rules.title: Subjunctive after il faut que
rules.rule: After il faut que, je veux que, pour que and similar, use the subjunctive: il faut que je parte.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.rule: The word exists but a French speaker would say something else here.

rules.title: Spelling and accents
rules.rule: Accents are part of the spelling and can change the meaning: a (has) vs à (to/at), ou (or) vs où (where).

rules.title: Capitals and punctuation
rules.rule: Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop or question mark. French puts a space before ? and !.

rules.title: Other mistakes
rules.rule: A mistake that does not fit the other rules.
